Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write the first page of an onboarding document for a new backend engineer joining a payments team. Around 200 words.

Welcome to the payments team. This document covers what you need before your first pull request touches money.

Payments processes roughly 40,000 transactions a day across three providers: Stripe for cards, Adyen for local rails in the EU, and an in-house ACH pipeline for US bank transfers. All three write to the same ledger table, `ledger_entries`, and that table is the source of truth. If a number in a dashboard disagrees with `ledger_entries`, the dashboard is wrong.

Every change you make here goes through the reconciliation job before it ships to more than 1% of traffic. Read `docs/reconciliation.md` on day one; it explains why we run a nightly diff against each provider's settlement file instead of trusting webhooks alone. Webhooks arrive out of order and sometimes twice. Code that assumes otherwise breaks reconciliation, and a broken reconciliation job means we can't tell finance how much money moved.

In your first two weeks, pair with your onboarding buddy on a ledger read path, then take a small write-path ticket under review from a second engineer. No one merges a change to the charge or refund flow with a single reviewer. This rule exists because a single-reviewer refund bug in 2024 double-refunded about 300 customers.

Ask questions in `#payments-eng` before guessing.

Add a section on who to ask for what.

Who to ask

Reconciliation breaks, or the nightly diff won't clear: ping Priya in `#payments-eng`. She owns `docs/reconciliation.md` and the settlement-file parsers. Stripe or Adyen account questions, rate limits, and webhook config go to Marcus. He holds the provider relationships and can get you sandbox credentials. ACH pipeline, NACHA file formatting, and bank cutoff times go to Dana. She built the in-house ACH service and knows which cutoffs are hard deadlines and which are soft.

For refund or charge flow review, your onboarding buddy is your first reviewer. The second reviewer rotates through the team calendar posted in the payments-eng channel topic. Ledger schema changes, or anything touching `ledger_entries` directly, need sign-off from that week's on-call lead, listed in PagerDuty. For access requests, provider dashboard logins, or anything blocking your setup, file a ticket in `#payments-eng` and tag your onboarding buddy so it doesn't sit unanswered.

output:
On-call rotation

The rotation is weekly, listed in PagerDuty, and covers the ledger and reconciliation job. If reconciliation fails to clear overnight, the on-call engineer triages before standup, not after. Handoff happens Monday at 10am in `#payments-eng` on Discord: the outgoing engineer posts any open issues and their current state.
